concerns.text: Task T020 implements a 'Spatial Split' (Eastern/Western US) and T028-T029 implement 'Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMM)', but the Spec (FR-004, FR-006) and Constitution (Principle VII) mandate a 'Temporal Split' (2015-2020/21/22) and 'Diebold-Mariano test'. The task order enforces a methodology that contradicts the foundational requirements, making the downstream tasks (T021-T023) semantically invalid for the intended spec.

Task T014 derives 'first arrival' for the Continental US, but the Plan (Summary) restricts the data scope to 'Lake Powell'. T019/T020 depend on T014's output, creating a data-flow dependency where the consumer (Modeling) expects Continental data while the producer (Pipeline) is constrained to a regional subset that cannot support the Continental split logic defined in T020.

Task T030 flags findings if 'mean absolute difference > 3 days', but the Spec (SC-003) requires flagging if variation exceeds '7 days'. This threshold mismatch in the task definition violates the success criteria dependency, rendering the validation step semantically incorrect relative to the spec.

Task T032 generates 'continental-scale maps' but the Plan and data pipeline are restricted to 'Lake Powell'. The task description implies an output scope that the upstream data tasks (T011-T015) cannot produce, creating a logical gap in the artifact flow.
